contracts.summary: Implemented every type of the spec 4.3 'Contracts' block in src/AnsiDemo/Contracts/ (Rgb.cs with PixelMode, PixelBuffer.cs, Frame.cs with Cell, DemoRandom.cs, DemoClock.cs, Effects.cs [FrameContext, EffectAttribute, IEffect, IPixelEffect, ICellEffect, ScrollerText], Scenes.cs [SceneSpec, SceneCue, TransitionAttribute, ITransition], Audio.cs [AudioFormat, Instrument, ISampleSource, ISynth, IAudioSink, AudioDeviceException], Song.cs [RowCell, Pattern, Song, SongFormatException]) with the exact signatures. Added tests in tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Contracts/ (Rgb, PixelBuffer, Frame, DemoRandom, Song, DemoClock, SceneSpec, BannedApi for N.1). Acceptance command passes (build 0 warnings, 67 tests passed).
contracts.notes:
- Namespace AnsiDemo.Contracts; signatures exactly as in spec 4.3, no extra public members.
- PixelBuffer and Frame constructors throw exactly ArgumentException (not a subclass) for non-positive sizes; PixelBuffer.SizeFor itself does not validate.
- Frame.CopyFrom throws ArgumentException (paramName "other") on size mismatch. Frame indexers clip (outside: get Blank / Black, set ignored); Frame.Write clips per character.
- Frame.ToAnsi uses ESC = \e, emits SGR 38;2 then 48;2 on change vs the previous cell in the same row (always at x = 0), row ends with "\e[0m\n". ToText trims trailing spaces only (' ').
- Rgb.Lerp/FromHsv round with MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero; FromHsv(0,0,0.5) = (128,128,128).
- DemoRandom.Next throws ArgumentException for a negative maxExclusive; Next(0) returns 0. Hash uses the formula as written; note Hash(-x,-y) can equal Hash(x,y).
- The N.1 test (BannedApiTests) scans src/AnsiDemo/Contracts/*.cs for \b(Console|Random|DateTime\w*|Stopwatch)\b, so the word 'Random' alone is banned there (DemoRandom is fine). Other modules can copy its FindRepoRoot pattern (walk up from [CallerFilePath] to AnsiDemo.slnx).

core-render.summary: I added the first half of core in src/AnsiDemo/Core/: HalfBlockRenderer, BrailleRenderer, Renderers, EffectCatalog, TransitionCatalog and Timeline, plus an internal helper AttributedTypes<TAttribute> that does the reflection lookup. I added Golden.Assert in tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Support/Golden.cs. Tests are in tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Core/: RendererTests, CatalogTests, TimelineTests, GoldenTests and BannedApiTests (the N.1 scan), along with the test classes TestPixelEffect, TestCellEffect and TestCutTransition. The acceptance command passes: build has 0 warnings and 66 Core tests pass. The full suite (134 tests) also passes. The renderers are checked to allocate 0 bytes per frame after the first one.
core-render.notes:
- Test classes already registered in the test assembly (namespace AnsiDemo.Tests.Core), which core-runners can reuse:
  - `[Effect("test-pixel", PixelMode.Braille)]` TestPixelEffect: fills the whole buffer with grey 128 + 32┬╖Time, capped at 255.
  - `[Effect("test-cell", PixelMode.HalfBlock)]` TestCellEffect: writes "TEST" in white on black at (0,0).
  - `[Transition("test-cut")]` TestCutTransition: copies `from` while progress < 0.5, else `to`.
  These names appear in EffectCatalog.Names and TransitionCatalog.Names whenever the test assembly is loaded. Never assert an exact list of names.
- Catalogs: each assembly whose name starts with "AnsiDemo" is scanned once (cached per assembly with a ConditionalWeakTable); the index is rebuilt on every call, so assemblies loaded later are picked up.
  - Unknown name: ArgumentException ("Unknown effect 'x'." or "Unknown transition 'x'.", paramName "name"). Name lookup is ordinal and case-sensitive.
  - A registered class that is abstract, lacks a public parameterless constructor or does not implement IEffect / ITransition: Create throws InvalidOperationException.
  - Two classes with the same name: InvalidOperationException.
- Renderers throw exactly ArgumentException (paramName "pixels") on a size mismatch. Renderers.Render throws ArgumentException for an undefined PixelMode.
- Timeline:
  - StartOf accepts index 0..scenes.Count (Count gives the total) and throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException otherwise.
  - Scene lengths are summed one scene at a time (Bars┬╖SecondsPerBar), so StartOf, TotalSeconds and CueAt boundaries are consistent bit for bit.
  - CueAt returns null for NaN, negative t, t ΓëÑ TotalSeconds and an empty list.
- Golden.Assert(frame, name, callerFile): ANSIDEMO_UPDATE_GOLDENS must be exactly "1" to overwrite. Failures throw Xunit.Sdk.FailException. Files are UTF-8 without BOM with '\n' line endings.
- I did not create SceneRunner, DemoRunner or Perf; core-runners adds them in src/AnsiDemo/Core/ and tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Support/Perf.cs.
- The Core N.1 test (tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Core/BannedApiTests.cs) scans src/AnsiDemo/Core/*.cs for \b(Console|Random|DateTime\w*|Stopwatch)\b, so the bare word "Random" is banned even in comments (DemoRandom is fine).

core-runners.summary: I finished the core module. I added `SceneRunner` and `DemoRunner` in `src/AnsiDemo/Core/` with the exact 4.3 signatures, and `Perf.MeanFrameMs` in `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Support/Perf.cs`. 47 new tests are in `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Core/` (SceneRunnerTests, DemoRunnerTests, PerfTests). They use new recording test effects (`test-rec-pixel`, `test-rec-cell`), a noise effect (`test-noise`) and a recording transition (`test-rec`). Together they cover 3.4ΓÇô3.7, 3.9 and Perf. They also check that `SceneRunner.Render` and `DemoRunner.Render` allocate nothing in the steady state. The acceptance command passes: the build has 0 warnings and all 113 Core tests pass. The full suite (319 tests) also passes.
core-runners.notes:
Behaviour you can rely on:

- **`SceneRunner`**
  - The constructor creates every layer through `EffectCatalog.Create` in script order and never touches `TransitionCatalog`. It resets layer i with `new DemoRandom((uint)(seed*31 + i + 1))` and a context with Time 0, DeltaTime 0. `Beats = Time * Bpm / 60.0`.
  - `Render(frame)`: clear to Black, pixel layers, `Renderers.Render`, then cell layers. It throws `ArgumentException` if the frame size is not the runner's cols├ùrows.
  - `Step(dt)` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for negative or NaN dt. `cols` or `rows` Γëñ 0 also throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
  - `Resize` resets every layer at the current Time with the same seeds and keeps Time.
  - `RenderAt` steps `(int)Math.Round(30*seconds)` times by `HeadlessStep`. It throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for negative, NaN or infinite seconds.
  - An internal helper, `SceneRunner.SteppedTo(scene, cols, rows, seconds, seed)`, returns the stepped runner without rendering. `DemoRunner.Seek` uses it.
- **`DemoRunner`**
  - Seed 1 for every scene. It copies the scene list. The constructor throws `ArgumentException` when `CueAt(scenes, 0)` is null, e.g. for an empty list.
  - The constructor applies the cue for t = 0: scene 0, plus a blank from-frame when scene 0 has `TransitionBars` > 0. So `Render` before the first `Step` shows the transition at progress 0.
  - **Design choice:** when `Step` enters a new scene, the new runner is created at scene time 0 and stepped by `cue.SceneTime` (not dt), so its Time equals the cue's SceneTime. The previous runner becomes the from-scene only when `cue.FromScene` equals the previous scene's index. It keeps stepping by dt until `cue.FromScene` is null, then it is dropped.
  - Past TotalSeconds, `Step` drops any from-scene and keeps stepping the last scene. `Render` never throws there.
  - `Seek(t)` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for negative or NaN t. For t ΓëÑ TotalSeconds it sets Time (so `Finished` is true) and keeps the current scene. Otherwise it builds only the cue's scene, stepped from its start in 1/30 s steps, with no from-scene and no transition. Stepping after a `Seek` also stays without a transition until the next scene change.
  - Each scene's transition is created once and cached, as soon as a transition into that scene starts. An unknown transition name therefore throws in the constructor or `Step`, not in `Render`.
  - `Render` throws `ArgumentException` if the frame size differs from the runner's.
  - `RenderAt` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when `CueAt` is null.
  - **Allocations:** `Render` allocates nothing in the steady state. `Step` still allocates one `FrameContext` per runner step and one `SceneCue` from `Timeline.CueAt`. Both are fixed-signature records, so this cannot be avoided.
- **`Perf.MeanFrameMs(effect, mode, cols, rows)`**: `SceneRunner` over `SceneSpec.Solo(effect, mode)`, 10 warm-up frames, then the mean milliseconds of `Step(HeadlessStep)` + `Render` over 60 frames, timed with Stopwatch.
- **New names in the catalogs** whenever the test assembly is loaded:
  - Effects `test-rec-pixel`, `test-rec-cell` and `test-noise`, all preferring HalfBlock.
  - Transition `test-rec`.
  - The recording ones add themselves to a static `TestLog`. They never throw and are safe to create from tests that loop over `EffectCatalog.Names`, but they keep accumulating log entries.

transitions.summary: I added the four transitions in src/AnsiDemo/Transitions/: CrossfadeTransition [Transition("crossfade")], WipeTransition ("wipe"), DissolveTransition ("dissolve") and PushTransition ("push"). Each is public sealed, has no state, has a parameterless constructor and implements the cell rules of spec 5.1-5.4. Their shared checks live in an internal static helper, TransitionInput: all three frames must be the same size (ArgumentException otherwise), progress is clamped to 0..1 with NaN treated as 0, and floor(progress┬╖Cols) is computed in one place. I added tests in tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Transitions/. There is one rule test file per transition, covering several progress values with frames whose characters and colours differ by position and between from and to. TransitionContractTests checks, for all four transitions: the attribute name, sealed/public/parameterless constructor, no fields, exactly `from` at 0 and below (including NaN and -Γê₧), exactly `to` at 1 and above, inputs left unchanged, an ArgumentException when the from, to or output frame alone has a different size, and no allocation in Apply. BannedApiTests is the N.1 scan of src/AnsiDemo/Transitions/*.cs, finding the repo root by walking up from [CallerFilePath]. TestFrames.cs is a frame-building helper for the tests. The acceptance command passes: build with 0 warnings, 91 Transitions tests passed.
transitions.notes:
- Classes are in namespace AnsiDemo.Transitions: CrossfadeTransition, WipeTransition, DissolveTransition, PushTransition. TransitionCatalog finds them through [Transition(name)] with the names "crossfade", "wipe", "dissolve" and "push". There is also an internal static helper, TransitionInput, which has no attribute and is not an ITransition.
- Apply(from, to, progress, output) throws ArgumentException when `to` or `output` is a different size from `from`; the frames are checked before progress is used. Progress is clamped to 0..1 and NaN counts as 0. Apply never allocates and only reads `from` and `to`.
- `output` should be a separate frame from `from` and `to`. Using the same object for both is not supported, and push in particular reads columns it may already have overwritten.
- Rows are handled independently (wipe and push work by column), so a blank frame from DemoRunner for FromScene = -1 works like any other frame.

audio-synth.summary: Added AnsiDemo.Audio.Synth (public sealed, parameterless ctor, implements ISynth) in src/AnsiDemo/Audio/Synth.cs, with internal helpers SynthChannel.cs (one oscillator plus envelope and LFSR) and SynthWaveform.cs (Pulse/Triangle/Noise enum). Channels 0 and 1 are pulse, 2 is triangle and 3 is noise. NoteOn resets phase, envelope and LFSR. Render writes (short)(clamp(0.25┬╖╬ú value┬╖Volume┬╖envelope, ΓêÆ1, 1)┬╖32767) for each sample, then advances every channel. It works in double math and allocates nothing. Invalid channel or frequency (Γëñ0, >22050, NaN) throws ArgumentException. Added tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Audio/SynthTests.cs with 47 test cases. The acceptance command passes: build has 0 warnings and all 47 tests pass.
audio-synth.notes:
- `new AnsiDemo.Audio.Synth()` is the only public type. SynthChannel and SynthWaveform are internal.
- Frequency is checked as `!(f > 0 && f <= 22050)`, so NaN and infinity also throw. A null instrument throws ArgumentNullException. A call that throws leaves the channel unchanged.
- SetFrequency on a channel that has had no NoteOn (or after NoteOff) only stores the pitch; the channel stays silent. NoteOff on an already-silent channel is allowed.
- Phase wraps by subtracting floor. The noise channel accumulates 16┬╖f/SampleRate per sample and steps the LFSR once per whole unit, up to 8 steps per sample at 22050 Hz. A silent channel does not advance.
- Volume is not clamped per channel; only the final mix is clamped. A 4-channel full-volume mix of ┬▒1 reaches exactly ┬▒32767.
- Test files written by this task: tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Audio/SynthTests.cs (namespace AnsiDemo.Tests.Audio).

audio-sinks.summary:
Added the audio sinks in AnsiDemo.Audio.
- WaveOutSink: winmm.dll calls through [DllImport] in WaveOutNative, with the WAVEFORMATEX and WAVEHDR structs (WaveOutFormat, WaveOutHeader). Each buffer's samples and header live in unmanaged memory (WaveOutBuffer).
- Start opens WAVE_MAPPER as 16-bit mono 44100 Hz and queues 4 buffers of 2048 samples inside Start itself. A background feeder thread then checks every 5 ms for WHDR_DONE and refills.
- Stop is idempotent and works from any thread: it joins the feeder for at most 250 ms, then calls waveOutReset, unprepares the headers, closes the device and frees the memory.
- WavFileSink renders exactly totalSamples in chunks of 4096 and writes a canonical 44-byte RIFF/WAVE header plus little-endian samples.
- NullSink never calls Render.
- Tests: WavFileSinkTests, NullSinkTests, WaveOutSinkTests and the fake source SinkTestSource. The device tests carry [Trait("Category","Device")] and return early when there is no device. They passed against a real device here.
- Acceptance command: build has 0 warnings, 18 sink tests pass; the full Audio suite is 65/65.
audio-sinks.notes:
- Public API is exactly as in spec 4.3: WaveOutSink() with static DeviceCount, WavFileSink(string path, long totalSamples), NullSink. Everything else (WaveOutNative, WaveOutFormat, WaveOutHeader, WaveOutBuffer) is internal.
- WaveOutSink can only be started once. A second Start throws InvalidOperationException, even after Stop. To restart (e.g. for --loop), create a new sink or just Seek the SongPlayer. Start after Dispose throws ObjectDisposedException.
- Start throws AudioDeviceException with Code 2 when DeviceCount is 0, or with the MMRESULT when waveOutOpen, waveOutPrepareHeader or waveOutWrite fails.
- The source's Render is called on the feeder thread, and also inside Start for the first 4 buffers. SongPlayer.Seek and Paused are set from the UI thread, so they must be thread-safe, as spec 8.6 already requires.
- If the source throws on the feeder thread, or the device disappears, playback silently ends instead of crashing the process. Stop still cleans up.
- WavFileSink(path, totalSamples): totalSamples must be ΓëÑ 0 and small enough to fit the 32-bit RIFF size, otherwise ArgumentOutOfRangeException. For --wav, pass totalSamples = round(TotalSeconds ┬╖ 44100). Start writes the file synchronously; Stop and Dispose do nothing.
- NullSink.Start accepts repeated calls; it only rejects a null source.

tracker.summary:
I added the tracker module in src/AnsiDemo/Tracker/ (namespace AnsiDemo.Tracker), one type per file:
- Notes.cs: Frequency is 440┬╖2^((midiΓêÆ69)/12). Parse accepts exactly [A-G](#|-)[0-8] and throws FormatException for anything else, including null.
- SongParser.cs: reads the line-based song format from spec 4.3. It handles comments, both line endings, all the directives and the cell grammar. Every violation throws SongFormatException with the 1-based line; problems only found at the end of the text use the last line.
- SongPlayer.cs: renders sample-accurately for any buffer split. Row starts are rounded from the absolute row index, so they don't drift, and arpeggio steps fall at 1/3 and 2/3 of each row. It also handles loop and end-of-song silence, Paused, a thread-safe Seek, and Position/Duration. The steady-state Render path doesn't allocate.

In tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Tracker/ I added RecordingSynth plus NotesTests, SongParserTests (a full valid song, and one theory per error kind asserting Line) and SongPlayerTests.

The acceptance command passes: the build has 0 warnings, and all 130 Tracker tests pass.
tracker.notes:
- The API matches spec 4.3: Notes.Frequency/Parse, SongParser.Parse, and SongPlayer(song, synth, loop) with PositionSeconds, DurationSeconds, Paused and Seek.
- Parser: the instrument directive needs its settings in the order `duty= vol= decay=`. Note letters are uppercase only and instrument and pattern names are case-sensitive. The arp hex digits after `a` may be upper or lower case. Tokens can be separated by spaces or tabs. An empty pattern (`pattern x` then `end`) is allowed. Error messages start with "Line N: ".
- SongPlayer: the constructor throws ArgumentException if a row doesn't have exactly 4 cells or a note has a bad instrument index or volume. Seek(NaN) throws ArgumentException. A seek is applied at the next Render even while paused, so the position moves but nothing is rendered. Seeking after a non-looping song has ended plays it again from the new row. Once a non-looping song ends, PositionSeconds stays at the end. With loop on, PositionSeconds wraps to 0.
- The arpeggio step at 1/3 of the row is always sent when (X, Y) Γëá (0, 0), even if X is 0.
- RecordingSynth has three members beyond the spec: CallSamples (the value of SamplesRendered when each call was made), Instruments (the instrument passed to every NoteOn) and a private setter on SamplesRendered. The Calls format is exactly as specified.
- At bpm 125 and 4 rows per beat a row is 5292 samples, and the arpeggio steps land at 1764 and 3528.

soundtrack.summary: Added src/AnsiDemo/Music/Soundtrack.cs: `public static class Soundtrack { public const string Text = """ΓÇª"""; }` in namespace AnsiDemo.Music. It holds a chiptune in A minor (Am F C G with a Dm E turnaround) at bpm 125 and rows-per-beat 4. It defines 9 instruments: lead, soft, arp, pad, bass, sub, kick, snare and hat. It has 23 distinct 2-bar (32-row) patterns, and its order list has 38 entries (76 bars = 145.92 s). Sections change exactly on the scene boundaries at bars 8, 18, 28, 36, 44, 54, 64 and 74. The arrangement: boot is a sparse intro that builds up; title is the theme with an echo; tunnel has arpeggio chords and a counter melody; fire has the theme an octave up, a driving bass and four-on-the-floor drums; roto reprises the theme; flight has harmony in thirds over half-time drums; mandel is a breakdown with pads that ends in a build-up; spheres is the finale over arpeggios; a 2-bar ending lets the final Am chord ring out. Channel roles: 0 lead, 1 arpeggios/echo/harmony (uses `v` and `a37`/`a47`), 2 triangle bass, 3 noise drums (kick C-2, snare D-5, hat C-8). Added tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Music/SoundtrackTests.cs with 11 tests. They check that the text parses (9.1); bpm, rows-per-beat and that the duration is at least DemoBars┬╖SecondsPerBar (9.1); that every pattern in the order is 2 bars; that there are at least 6 distinct patterns (9.2); per-channel note counts of at least 100 (theory over 0..3) (9.2); that `v` and `a` are used (9.2); and a full render through `new SongPlayer(song, new Synth(), loop: false)` in 2048-sample chunks, asserting a clip ratio below 1% and a peak of at least 8000 (9.3). Measured over the whole song: peak about 20,400 and no samples at full scale. RMS per scene is 3,000-6,000, quieter in the intro and breakdown and loudest in the finale.
soundtrack.notes: The only API is AnsiDemo.Music.Soundtrack.Text (a const string). Parse it with AnsiDemo.Tracker.SongParser.Parse and play it with new SongPlayer(song, synth, loop). Song.DurationSeconds is 145.92 s (76 bars). That is 2 bars longer than DemoClock.DemoBars (74 bars = 142.08 s) because of a 2-bar ending pattern. For --wav, use the demo's TotalSeconds for the sample count (spec 10.7), not the song's duration. Every pattern is 32 rows (2 bars at 1.92 s per bar), so seeking the song to Timeline.StartOf(i) lands exactly on a pattern start for every scene.

effect-plasma.summary:
I added the plasma effect in `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Plasma/PlasmaEffect.cs`: `[Effect("plasma", PixelMode.HalfBlock)]`, a sealed `IPixelEffect`. It adds four sines: one of x, one of y, one of x+y, and one of the distance to a centre that moves on a slow Lissajous path. The sum indexes a 256-entry hue palette that repeats around the colour wheel. Update rebuilds the palette from 256 FromHsv calls, with saturation 0.85 and value between 0.75 and 1, so no pixel is ever black. The palette's hue shifts 30┬░ per second, so the full cycle takes 12 s.

Update precomputes the per-column, per-row, per-diagonal and squared-distance terms and the palette. Reset allocates them and calls the same step, so the t = 0 frame is ready right after Reset. Render indexes `pixels.Pixels` directly and uses a 1024-entry sine table, so it does not allocate. In Debug at 200├ù60 a frame takes well under 1 ms.

The effect uses `rng` only in Reset, to draw four phase offsets. The runner resets with the same seed on resize, so the picture does not jump.

Tests are in `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Plasma/PlasmaEffectTests.cs` and cover:
- 4.1: the same call twice gives identical ANSI output.
- 4.2: goldens t0, t1 and t4.
- 4.3: t = 1 differs from t = 0, and `LitCount` is at least 1152.
- 4.4: both modes at 80├ù24 and 200├ù60.
- 4.5: the Perf test.
- N.1: a scan of the Plasma folder for banned APIs.

They also check the preferred mode, the hue cycling and a resize. I recorded the three goldens and checked them: they show smooth colour blobs, and the hue shifts across t0, t1 and t4. The acceptance command passes with 0 warnings and 14 of 14 tests.
effect-plasma.notes: Effect name "plasma", class `AnsiDemo.Effects.Plasma.PlasmaEffect`, preferred mode HalfBlock. It writes every pixel with a bright, saturated colour, so it works as an opaque background, for example under the scroller in scene `title`. Its look depends only on scene time and the seed. Its goldens are in `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Plasma/t0.ansi`, `t1.ansi` and `t4.ansi`.

effect-fire.summary: I added the `fire` effect in `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Fire/FireEffect.cs`: `[Effect("fire", PixelMode.HalfBlock)] public sealed class FireEffect : IPixelEffect` in namespace `AnsiDemo.Effects.Fire`. It is the classic heat buffer. It runs 30 fixed ticks per second from the accumulated DeltaTime; catch-up is capped at 1 s, and there is a small epsilon so that headless steps give exactly one tick. Each tick puts random heat into two hidden seed rows below the bottom edge. Each seed column flips between hot and cold on rng draws, which makes the flames flicker. Then every cell takes the average of 3 cells in the row below plus 1 cell two rows below, minus a cooling term. That term is set from the simulation height so that no heat can survive above 85% of the height, plus a random jitter from a table filled from the rng. The simulation is never more than 60 rows tall: the scale is ceil(H/60), so 80├ù48 at 80├ù24 HalfBlock and 100├ù60 at 200├ù60 in both modes. `Render` scales it up bilinearly with maps precomputed in Reset and draws through a 256-entry palette (black ΓåÆ red ΓåÆ yellow ΓåÆ white) built once per instance. Render writes every pixel without allocating. Reset pre-warms with 2┬╖(height+2) ticks. In `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Fire/FireEffectTests.cs` there are 18 tests: 4.1 determinism, the t0/t1/t4 goldens (4.2), 4.3 (the frame changes and LitCount ΓëÑ 39), 4.4 for both modes at both sizes, the top 2 cell rows being black at t = 0, 1 and 4 in all 4 mode/size combinations, the bottom row burning, preferred mode HalfBlock, 4.5 perf with `[Trait("Category","Perf")]` (Γëñ 33 ms), and the N.1 source scan. I recorded the goldens `t0.ansi`, `t1.ansi` and `t4.ansi` and checked them with an ASCII heat dump. They show a white/yellow base and orange-red tongues of uneven height with dark-red tips that reach about 60% of the height, and the top third is black. The acceptance command passes: the build has 0 warnings and all 18 tests pass.
effect-fire.notes: The scene `fire` (HalfBlock, effect `fire`) can use the effect as-is. It is fully opaque: it writes every pixel and draws black where there is no flame. The top ~15% of the rows are always black, and the flames typically reach about half to two thirds of the height. The effect keeps no static state; the palette is an instance field. Resize calls Reset, which pre-warms again, so the flames look the same right after a resize. The goldens are at `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Fire/t{0,1,4}.ansi`.

effect-tunnel.summary:
I added `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Tunnel/TunnelEffect.cs`, declared as `[Effect("tunnel", PixelMode.HalfBlock)] public sealed class TunnelEffect : IPixelEffect`. It is a textured tunnel that rotates, flies forward and is darker toward the centre.

How it works:
- **Reset** builds a 64├ù64 texture: tiles in a checker of two hues with an XOR pattern inside and grey grout between them. No texel is black. The base hue comes from the given `DemoRandom`.
- **Lookup tables:** Reset also precomputes, per entry, the angle, the depth (k/distance) and a shade that falls toward the centre. The tables cover 2W├ù2H, so Render can move the tunnel centre around with an integer offset instead of recomputing them. The aspect ratio is corrected from ctx.
- **Update** only stores `ctx.Time`.
- **Render** derives the rotation, the forward movement and the centre's offset from the stored time, then does one lookup per pixel straight into `pixels.Pixels`. It allocates nothing and never indexes past either buffer.

I added `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Tunnel/TunnelEffectTests.cs` with 14 tests:
- 4.1: the same frame rendered twice gives identical output.
- 4.2: goldens t0, t1 and t4 at 80├ù24 HalfBlock.
- 4.3: the t = 1 frame differs from t = 0, with at least 1152 cells lit.
- 4.4: both modes at 80├ù24 and 200├ù60.
- Extra: the preferred mode is HalfBlock, and rendering works after a resize.
- 4.5: a Perf test (`[Trait("Category", "Perf")]`) with a 33 ms budget at 200├ù60.
- N.1: a scan of the source files for banned APIs.

I recorded the three goldens and read them back as luma maps:
- **Lit cells:** 1912 of 1920 cells are lit; only a small disc at the vanishing point is dark.
- **Look:** the tiles show clear perspective and get gradually brighter toward the edges, and the centre moves between frames.
- **Colours:** gold and cyan tiles with grey grout.

The perf test runs 70 frames in about 27 ms, so well under 1 ms per frame. The acceptance command passes: build with 0 warnings and 14 of 14 tests. No `*.actual.ansi` files were left behind.
effect-tunnel.notes:
- **Effect name:** `tunnel`, class `AnsiDemo.Effects.Tunnel.TunnelEffect`, preferred mode HalfBlock. It writes every pixel, so it works as the background layer of scene `tunnel`, with `cube` drawn on top.
- **Moving centre:** the tunnel centre moves around (about ┬▒16% of the width and ┬▒14% of the height), and only a small disc at the centre is black.
- **Braille:** the effect works in Braille mode, but the area near the centre comes out sparsely dithered because it is dark.
- **Goldens:** `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Tunnel/t0.ansi`, `t1.ansi` and `t4.ansi`.

effect-starfield.summary: Added `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Starfield/StarfieldEffect.cs`, a sparse `IPixelEffect` registered as `[Effect("starfield", PixelMode.Braille)]`. The number of stars is max(200, pixel area / 64), so 240 at 80├ù24 Braille and 1500 at 200├ù60. Each star is an (x, y, z) point projected in perspective from the buffer centre, with z falling at a slightly varying speed. A star that leaves the buffer or reaches the near plane respawns at the far plane, at a random point in the central 60% of the buffer, using the kept `DemoRandom`. In Reset, star depths follow the distribution a running starfield settles into, so the t = 0 frame already looks like any later frame. Colour goes from grey (160 in Braille, 80 in HalfBlock) when far to white when near. Near stars are drawn as streaks pointing outward from the centre that fade toward the tail, or as two pixels side by side when the streak is shorter than one pixel. Only star pixels are written. Render does not allocate and returns without drawing if the buffer size does not match. Added `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Starfield/StarfieldEffectTests.cs` (15 tests) covering catalog registration, 4.1, 4.2 (the goldens t0/t1/t4.ansi are recorded and were checked by viewing them), 4.3, 4.4 in both modes at both sizes, resize, sparseness in both modes (most pixels of a pre-filled buffer are kept and every star pixel is grey), 4.5 perf (Category Perf) and the N.1 scan of the source files. The acceptance command passes: the build has 0 warnings and all 15 tests pass.
effect-starfield.notes: The effect is `AnsiDemo.Effects.Starfield.StarfieldEffect`, named "starfield", with Braille as its preferred mode. It writes only star pixels (greys and white) and leaves every other pixel as it found it, so in the `flight` scene it can be drawn first as the sky and voxel draws over it. In HalfBlock mode far stars use a darker grey (80) than in Braille (160), because no dithering threshold applies there.

effect-rotozoomer.summary: Added `RotozoomerEffect` (`[Effect("rotozoomer", PixelMode.HalfBlock)]`, an `IPixelEffect` that writes every pixel) in `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Rotozoomer/`. `Reset` builds a 64├ù64 tileable texture: warm and cool checkerboard quadrants with an XOR colour gradient, a bright ring and a centre dot in each quadrant, a purple grid line and a small grain taken from the given `DemoRandom`. No texel is black. `Update`/`Reset` turn the scene time into an angle (a 0.35 rad offset plus 0.45 rad/s plus a wobble), a zoom of 1.1 ┬▒ 0.75┬╖sin(0.9t) and a drifting centre. The results are stored as 16.16 fixed-point per-pixel and per-row steps. `Render` walks `pixels.Pixels` with integer adds and masks the texture coordinates. It allocates nothing and does not change state. The scale and aspect are normalised to the pixel height and the cell shape, so the picture looks the same in both modes and at every size. The tests in `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Rotozoomer/RotozoomerEffectTests.cs` cover 4.1, 4.2 (t0/t1/t4 goldens recorded and checked: the tiles are rotated about 20┬░, 53┬░ and 145┬░ at different zooms), 4.3 (`LitCount` is 100%), 4.4, keeping working after a resize, 4.5 (Perf trait) and the N.1 source scan. The acceptance command passes: 0 warnings and 14/14 tests.
effect-rotozoomer.notes: Effect name `rotozoomer`, prefers HalfBlock, and every pixel is non-black in every frame. The picture is a function of scene time only: the `rng` passed to `Reset` only adds a fixed grain to the texture, so resizing with the same seed gives the same texture. Goldens: `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Rotozoomer/t0.ansi`, `t1.ansi`, `t4.ansi`. In Braille mode the cool blue tiles have low luma, so they dither sparsely. That is acceptable because the demo shows it only in HalfBlock (scene `roto`).

effect-cube.summary:
I added `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Cube/CubeEffect.cs` with `[Effect("cube", PixelMode.Braille)] public sealed class CubeEffect : IPixelEffect`. It is a wireframe cube with 8 vertices and 12 edges. It rotates about X at 0.9 rad/s and about Y at 0.55 rad/s, both with phase offsets, and is projected in perspective with the camera at distance 4. The focal length is 0.85 ├ù min(pixel width, pixel height) and the cube is centred; pixels are square in both modes, so one scale serves both axes. The projected cube spans about 57ΓÇô82% of the height and stays inside the buffer.

Edges are Bresenham lines; pixels outside the buffer are skipped. In Braille mode the lines are 2 pixels thick. The colour is `Rgb.FromHsv(45┬░┬╖t, 0.4, 1)`, a low saturation that keeps the luma high. The fill is sparse: only edge pixels are written. Projection and colour are computed in Reset and Update. Render only draws and does not allocate. The vertex and edge tables are static `ReadOnlySpan` data, so there is no static mutable state.

The tests are in `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Cube/CubeEffectTests.cs`, 20 cases:
- catalog registration
- 4.1 determinism
- 4.2 goldens t0, t1 and t4 at 80├ù24 in Braille
- 4.3 the t = 1 frame differs from t = 0 and LitCount ΓëÑ 39
- 4.4 both modes at 80├ù24 and 200├ù60
- 4.5 perf, with `[Trait("Category", "Perf")]`
- lit rows span ΓëÑ 1/3 of the height and never touch the frame edge, sampled every 7 steps up to 12 s in both modes and both sizes
- the edge colour changes with time
- sparseness on a pre-filled buffer in both modes
- N.1 source scan

I viewed the goldens and they show a clear rotating perspective cube. The three `.ansi` goldens are recorded, and there are no `*.actual.ansi` files. The acceptance command passes: the build has 0 warnings and 20/20 tests pass.
effect-cube.notes: Effect name `cube`, class `AnsiDemo.Effects.Cube.CubeEffect`, preferred mode Braille. The fill is sparse: it writes only edge pixels and never clears the buffer, so it can be layered over `tunnel` in HalfBlock scenes. The size scales with min(PixelWidth, PixelHeight), and the cube stays inside the buffer at any size. Lines are 2 px thick only in Braille mode and 1 px thick in HalfBlock. It uses no randomness: the `DemoRandom` passed to Reset is ignored.

effect-metaballs.summary: Added `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Metaballs/MetaballsEffect.cs`: `[Effect("metaballs", PixelMode.Braille)]` IPixelEffect with 6 balls on Lissajous paths (radii, amplitudes, speeds and phases drawn from the rng in Reset; horizontal phases spread evenly so ΓëÑ4 blobs are usually distinct while paths still cross the centre). Field ╬ú r┬▓/d┬▓ in square-pixel units scaled by buffer height, evaluated with a field-weighted tint on a half-resolution grid in Reset/Update; Render only reads it, bilinearly interpolates the field per pixel, and writes every pixel: black below 0.6, a linear tinted glow up to 1.0, then a core whitening from 45% to 90% so Braille interiors are solid with a dithered coloured edge. Ball hues drift 24┬░/s. Added `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Metaballs/MetaballsEffectTests.cs` (4.1 determinism, 4.2 goldens t0/t1/t4, 4.3 change + LitCount ΓëÑ 39, 4.4 both modes at 80├ù24/200├ù60 plus an odd size and a resize, 4.5 Perf trait Γëñ 33 ms, N.1 banned-API scan) and the three recorded goldens. The acceptance command passes (15/15); perf measures ~2.6 ms/frame at 200├ù60 in Debug.
effect-metaballs.notes: Effect name `metaballs`, class `AnsiDemo.Effects.Metaballs.MetaballsEffect`, preferred mode Braille, fills all pixels (black outside the blobs), so in scene `boot` it is a full background layer under the Matrix cell effect. Render returns without drawing if the buffer size differs from the size given to Reset (it never throws). Goldens: `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Metaballs/t0.ansi`, `t1.ansi`, `t4.ansi` (80├ù24 Braille, seed 1).

effect-scroller.summary:
I added the `scroller` effect as `ScrollerEffect` in `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Scroller/ScrollerEffect.cs`. It is a cell effect with `[Effect("scroller", PixelMode.HalfBlock)]` and implements `ICellEffect`.

How it works:
- **Text:** `ScrollerText.Value` scrolls right to left at a constant 24 columns/s, repeats endlessly, and fills the full width at t = 0.
- **Wave:** each column's character sits at row centre + A┬╖sin(x┬╖2╧Ç/56 + 2.6┬╖t). The wave fills the middle third of the rows (rows/3 .. 2┬╖rows/3 ΓêÆ 1), so A = 3.5 at 24 rows and it grows with the row count.
- **Colour:** each character gets a bright, fully saturated HSV colour from its index in the text (9┬░ per character). The colours are worked out once in `Reset`.
- **Background:** spaces are skipped. Under a letter, the cell keeps its existing background at 35% brightness, so the plasma shows through in scene `title`.
- **State:** it depends only on time, so a resize lands at the right scroll position. `Render` allocates nothing.

Tests are in `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Scroller/ScrollerEffectTests.cs` (19 tests). They cover:
- 4.1 determinism
- 4.2 goldens `t0`/`t1`/`t4`, recorded, viewed and committed
- 4.3 the t = 1 frame differs from t = 0 and has at least 39 lit cells
- 4.4 both modes at 80├ù24 and 200├ù60
- 4.5 the perf test
- letters only in the middle third (both modes, several sizes)
- the wave spanning at least 6 rows
- scroll speed between 20 and 30 columns/s, found as the column shift between t = 1 and t = 2
- the column letters at t = 0 matching `ScrollerText.Value`
- the colour depending on the character's position
- N.1, a scan of the effect folder for banned APIs

The acceptance command passes: the build has 0 warnings and all 19 tests pass.
effect-scroller.notes:
- **Effect:** `scroller`, class `AnsiDemo.Effects.Scroller.ScrollerEffect`, preferred mode HalfBlock.
- **Rows used:** it only writes cells in rows rows/3 .. 2┬╖rows/3 ΓêÆ 1, one character per column, and never writes spaces.
- **Background:** under a letter it keeps the existing cell's background at 35% brightness, so the layers below (e.g. plasma in scene `title`) show around and behind the letters.
- **Scroll position:** floor(24┬╖t + 1e-9) mod text length, a pure function of scene time. Resize and Seek therefore give the same picture as continuous stepping.
- **Randomness:** none is used, so the seed does not change the output.

effect-mandelbrot.summary:
I added `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Mandelbrot/MandelbrotEffect.cs`, which is `[Effect("mandelbrot", PixelMode.HalfBlock)] MandelbrotEffect : IPixelEffect`. It is a continuous zoom into seahorse valley (ΓêÆ0.743643887037151 + 0.131825904205330i). The view drifts from the whole set at t = 0 onto the target, with the offset shrinking as zoomΓü╗┬▓. Outside the set it uses smooth colouring (n + 1 ΓêÆ log2(log|z|), bailout 256), mapped through a 512-entry cyclic palette built in Reset with cosine easing, and the palette cycles slowly with time. Inside the set is black, and it skips the main cardioid and period-2 bulb with the closed-form test. The iteration cap grows with zoom from 64 to 288. Large buffers are computed in blocks of at most 12 000 samples and scaled up; for 200├ù60 HalfBlock that is half horizontal resolution.

One deliberate change from the hint: the zoom ping-pongs at 2^17, not 2^40. Above about 2^20 this point needs hundreds to over 1000 iterations per pixel, so with any affordable cap the frame turns completely black (measured 0 lit cells at 2^40 with a cap of 160). At 2^17 a cap of 288 still shows detail, and the worst frame at 200├ù60 takes about 12 ms in Debug.

The tests (`tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Mandelbrot/MandelbrotEffectTests.cs`, 19 cases) cover:
- 4.1 determinism.
- 4.2 goldens t0/t1/t4.
- 4.3 the t = 1 frame differs from t = 0 and is lit.
- 4.4 both modes at 80├ù24 and 200├ù60, plus resize.
- 4.5 perf: `Perf.MeanFrameMs` is about 1 ms, and single frames at t = 19 s and at the deepest zoom stay within 33 ms and are lit.
- The zoom factor at 20 s is ΓëÑ 1024, and the zoom is continuous and turns back.
- Deep frames have detail.
- N.1 source scan.

I converted the three goldens to PNGs and checked them: the whole set with bands at t0, the zoom into the valley by t4. I also looked at frames at 10, 19, 28 and 40 s, which show seahorse detail. The acceptance command passes: build with 0 warnings, 19/19 tests.
effect-mandelbrot.notes:
Effect name `mandelbrot`, preferred mode HalfBlock, class `AnsiDemo.Effects.Mandelbrot.MandelbrotEffect`.
- Public helpers: `static double ZoomFactor(double time)`, which is 2^(0.6┬╖t) ping-ponging between 1 and 2^17 (2^11.5 at the end of the 19.2 s `mandel` scene, 2^12 at 20 s); `const ZoomOctavesPerSecond = 0.6`; `const MaxZoomOctaves = 17`.
- The picture depends only on scene time: `Update` stores `ctx.Time`, and `Render` computes from it without allocating.
- The effect ignores its `DemoRandom`.
- It writes every pixel; the inside of the set is `Rgb.Black`.

effect-voxel.summary: Added `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Voxel/VoxelEffect.cs`, which is `[Effect("voxel", PixelMode.HalfBlock)] public sealed class VoxelEffect : IPixelEffect`. In Reset it builds a tileable 256├ù256 heightmap from five octaves of value noise seeded by the rng. It also builds a colour map that goes green ΓåÆ brown ΓåÆ white by height, with slope lighting and a little grain, and allocates a y-buffer for each column. Each frame the camera flies forward along a gently swerving sine path that depends only on time. Its altitude is set to clear the terrain about 1.5 s ahead. For each screen column the effect marches front to back with a step that grows with distance and projects the bilinear height with perspective. It draws vertical spans upward from the y-buffer and blends the colour toward a blue-grey fog with distance. The horizon is at 45% of the height, and terrain is never drawn above the top 15%, so the sky stays untouched. At 200├ù60 in Debug a frame takes about 1 ms. Added `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Voxel/VoxelEffectTests.cs` with 15 tests: determinism (4.1), goldens t0/t1/t4 (4.2), animation and LitCount ΓëÑ 39 (4.3), both modes at 80├ù24 and 200├ù60 (4.4), the Perf budget of 33 ms or less (4.5), sky untouched with ground drawn, and the N.1 banned-API scan. The sky test renders straight onto a magenta-filled buffer every second over 10 s: the top 10% of rows must keep the colour and the bottom 10% must not. I recorded the goldens, turned them into images to check them against the 'Must look like' line, adjusted the effect, and recorded them again. They show a green valley, brown slopes, snow-capped peaks fading into fog, and a black sky band. The acceptance command passes: 0 warnings, 15 of 15 tests pass.
effect-voxel.notes: The `voxel` effect only writes landscape pixels. Everything above the terrain line is left as it was, and the top 15% of the pixel height is never written at any time. In scene `flight` the starfield therefore shows through the sky band. The horizon sits at 45% of the height. Distant terrain fades to a fog colour, Rgb(86, 98, 128), so a hazy horizon line is visible against the stars. All state depends only on ctx.Time and the rng, so a Reset on resize at the current time gives a consistent picture. If Render gets a buffer whose size differs from the last Reset, it draws nothing instead of throwing. The goldens are at `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Voxel/t0.ansi`, `t1.ansi` and `t4.ansi`.

effect-raymarch.notes:
The effect is `raymarch` in `AnsiDemo.Effects.Raymarch.RaymarchEffect`, preferring Braille, for the final `spheres` scene.
- It overwrites every pixel, so it must be the back layer.
- It uses one value from the DemoRandom passed to Reset, the orbiter's starting phase. A Resize therefore keeps the same picture.
- Only RaymarchEffect.cs, the test file and the goldens t0.ansi, t1.ansi and t4.ansi were added. No shared files were touched.

effect-matrix.summary: I added `src/AnsiDemo/Effects/Matrix/MatrixEffect.cs` (`[Effect("matrix", PixelMode.Braille)]`, an `ICellEffect`). Each column has one drop with its own speed (6-25 rows/s), tail length (5 to 3/4 of the rows) and fractional head position. Glyphs come from a cols├ùrows grid of random ASCII 33..126 and keep changing: the head writes a new glyph into each row it enters, and about 1/120 of the grid is re-rolled every tick. The head is near white (210,255,210) and the tail fades from bright green to black. Glyph cells have Bg = Black and every other cell is left as it was. The effect runs in fixed 1/60 s ticks built from accumulated DeltaTime, so the result does not depend on frame rate. A drop that leaves the bottom respawns above the top after a random gap, and Reset starts the drops at random heights, so the t = 0 frame already shows rain. I added `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Effects/Matrix/MatrixEffectTests.cs` with 22 tests: 4.1-4.5, N.1, printable glyphs on black with green tails, one fading drop per column with a near-white head, varied fall speeds, glyphs changing, results independent of step size, and cells outside the drops left untouched. I also recorded, viewed and added the t0, t1 and t4 goldens. The acceptance command passes: 0 warnings, 22/22 tests.
effect-matrix.notes: Effect name "matrix", preferred mode Braille, class AnsiDemo.Effects.Matrix.MatrixEffect. It only writes the cells of its drops, with Bg = Black, so the metaballs underneath in scene `boot` show between the columns. Near the end of a tail the glyphs can have Fg equal to Black, so they look blank and hide the cell below. Reset reinitialises all state from the given rng, also on resize, and does not use ctx.Time. The simulation advances only through accumulated DeltaTime.

shell-options.summary: I added src/AnsiDemo/Shell/DemoScript.cs, which holds the 8-row scene table of spec 4.3 (74 bars), and AppOptions.cs with the record from the spec. I also added AppOptionsParser.cs: it has the four-line Usage constant joined with '\n', and Parse accepts exactly the three usage forms. Every error throws ArgumentException whose message is Usage. The tests are in tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Demo/: DemoScriptTests checks each scene field by field, the 74-bar and TotalSeconds totals, that every transition is registered and that the lists are read-only. AppOptionsParserTests covers the defaults, every valid form and every error case with the message equal to Usage, plus the usage text line by line. AppOptionsTestEffect.cs registers the [Effect("test-options", HalfBlock)] test effect. The acceptance command passes: the build has 0 warnings and 95 filtered tests pass. The full suite (367 tests) also passes.
shell-options.notes:
- `AnsiDemo.Shell.AppOptionsParser` also exposes `public const int DefaultCols = 80, DefaultRows = 24`. `Parse(null)` throws ArgumentNullException. Every other error throws `new ArgumentException(Usage)`, so `ex.Message == Usage` exactly. HeadlessHost and Program can catch ArgumentException, write Usage to stderr and exit 2.
- The parser does not check the upper bound of `--frame`: any finite value ΓëÑ 0 is accepted, so the host must turn ArgumentOutOfRangeException from RenderAt into the usage message and exit 2. `--frame -0` is accepted as 0.
- A value is treated as missing when it is absent, empty or starts with "--" (e.g. `--scene --loop` is an error). The parser accepts flags in any order.
- Defaults are Cols 80 and Rows 24, even when `--size` is not given. `Wav` is the raw path string; the parser does not touch the file system.
- Scene names are checked against `DemoScript.Scenes[i].Name` and effect names against `EffectCatalog.Names` (ordinal). The `--effect` check uses the catalog at parse time, so real effects are found once their modules are merged.
- The test effect "test-options" (class `AnsiDemo.Tests.Demo.AppOptionsTestEffect`, an ICellEffect that writes "OPTIONS" at (0,0)) is now in EffectCatalog.Names whenever the test assembly is loaded. Do not assert an exact list of names.
- `DemoScript.Scenes` and each scene's `Effects` are read-only collection-expression lists that are created once (the same instance is returned on every call).

headless-host.notes:
- On a usage error, HeadlessHost writes `AppOptionsParser.Usage` with `stderr.WriteLine` (so Usage plus a newline), flushes, writes nothing to stdout and returns 2.
- On success it does `stdout.Write(frame.ToAnsi())` and then `Flush()`.
- **Program must pass the stdout writer:** the writer should encode UTF-8 without a BOM, e.g. `new StreamWriter(Console.OpenStandardOutput(), new UTF8Encoding(false))`. HeadlessHost never touches `Console`.
- **Precedence:** if `o.Wav` is set it wins over everything else. Otherwise `o.Frame` must be set, or the result is exit 2.
- **Extra usage-error cases** (beyond the spec's list), for hand-built options: Scene and Effect both set, and Cols or Rows Γëñ 0.
- **Range checks:**
  - With scene or effect, t must satisfy 0 Γëñ t < Bars┬╖SecondsPerBar. For an effect that is 1920 s, because Solo has 1000 bars.
  - For the whole demo, HeadlessHost relies on DemoRunner.RenderAt throwing ArgumentOutOfRangeException.
- **WAV I/O errors** (e.g. a bad path) are not caught; they propagate to the caller.
- **New test effect name:** "test-headless" (class AnsiDemo.Tests.Demo.HeadlessHostTestEffect, IPixelEffect) is now registered in EffectCatalog.Names whenever the test assembly is loaded.

console-host.notes:
- **Wiring in Program.cs:** with no `--frame` or `--wav`, call `return AnsiDemo.Shell.ConsoleHost.Run(options);`. It returns 0 on quit or when the demo finishes and 1 when something throws. It writes its own messages to stderr after the terminal is restored, so Program should not wrap it in a catch that prints again.
- **Error cases:** if stdout is not a console (redirected), Run fails with exit 1 and the message "The output is not a console; use --frame to render without one." If `--scene` names an unknown scene it throws ArgumentException, which also becomes exit 1. The parser already rejects unknown names, so this should not happen in practice.
- **Public helpers you can reuse:**
  - `ConsoleFrameWriter`: `Append`, `AppendTooSmall`, `TooSmallMessage`, `IsTooSmall`, and `MinCols`/`MinRows` (80/24).
  - `ConsoleKeyMap.CommandFor`, returning the `ConsoleCommand` enum.
  - `ConsolePlayback`: `ForDemo`, `ForScene` and `SceneStartFrom`.
  - `ConsoleSession` and `ConsoleNative` are internal.
- **Key bindings for the README:** Q or Esc quits, Ctrl+C also quits, Space pauses and resumes, Left/Right go to the previous/next scene. Left and Right do nothing with `--scene` or `--effect`.
- **Behaviour choices:**
  - `--loop` restarts with `DemoRunner.Seek(0)`, so a restart shows scene 0 without its fade-in from blank.
  - With `--scene` or `--effect`, `--loop` and `--no-sound` are ignored.
  - If the window starts out smaller than 80x24, the runner is created at 80x24 and resized once the window is large enough.
- **Test effect:** "test-console" (`AnsiDemo.Tests.Demo.ConsoleTestEffect`) is now in `EffectCatalog.Names` whenever the test assembly is loaded.

demo-final.summary:
The demo is wired up and runnable, and the acceptance command passes: the build has 0 warnings and all 924 tests pass. Live playback with keys and sound has not been tried, because this environment has no interactive terminal.

- **Program.cs:** replaced the placeholder. It parses the arguments; on `ArgumentException` it writes the usage to stderr and returns 2. With `--frame` or `--wav` it runs `HeadlessHost` through a UTF-8 writer without a BOM and never touches the console. Otherwise it returns `ConsoleHost.Run(options)`.
- **DemoGoldenTests.cs:** records `scene<i>-mid` and `scene<i>-in` for all 8 scenes and checks that each `-in` frame has `LitCount() > 0`. I recorded the 16 goldens, rendered them to images and checked each one:
  - The mid frames show the right transition into each scene: blankΓåÆboot crossfade, bootΓåÆtitle dissolve, titleΓåÆtunnel wipe, tunnelΓåÆfire crossfade, fireΓåÆroto push, rotoΓåÆflight dissolve, flightΓåÆmandel crossfade and mandelΓåÆspheres wipe.
  - Each `-in` frame shows its own scene.
- **DemoIntegrationTests.cs** checks that:
  - the script uses exactly 12 distinct effects, and every effect and transition name resolves through the catalogs;
  - `--frame 20` writes exactly `DemoRunner.RenderAt(...,20).ToAnsi()` and returns 0;
  - `--frame` with each real `--scene` and `--effect` gives the matching `SceneRunner` frame;
  - `--frame` at TotalSeconds returns 2 and prints the usage;
  - N.2: a frame in the middle of each scene's transition, and the last frame of the demo, each finish within 10 s.
- **ReadmeTests.cs:** checks that the README lists every flag, every key, every scene and the exact usage text.
- **README.md:** rewritten. It describes the demo and its requirements, how to run it with examples, a table of the flags with the rules on combining them, the usage text, the keys, the scene table, the effect names, how goldens work and how to view one with `Get-Content`, and the test commands.

Other checks:
- `--frame 20` printed 24 rows with no BOM; `--frame 142.08` and an unknown flag each print the usage and exit 2.
- `--wav` wrote 12,531,500 bytes (44 + 2┬╖6,265,728) in about 1 s; the file was deleted afterwards.
- With output redirected, the console host exits 1 with "The output is not a console; use --frame to render without one."

No integration bugs in the hosts and no problems in other modules turned up, so no files under `Shell/` changed.
